quote: Most that I have done and suffered in the service of our cause has been in public, and I have received much encouragement at every step of the way. You on the other hand have labored in a private way.
source: Frederick Douglass, letter to Harriet Tubman, 29 August 1868, in Sarah H. Bradford, Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman, p. 7 (1869)
note: Corrected the page. The letter begins at the foot of page 6 in the 1869 Auburn printing and these two sentences fall on page 7. Bradford’s book is named as the printing that carries the letter. The wording is exact, including on the other hand without commas.

evidence.where: a transcription of the 1869 Auburn printing with its page break markers, read from the salutation to the signature
evidence.edition: Sarah H. Bradford, Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman, Auburn, W. J. Moses, Printer, 1869
evidence.locator: the letter headed Rochester, August 29, 1868; page 7 begins at kind lady, and that the same is so soon to be published

reason: The two sentences stand word for word in the letter, immediately after The difference between us is very marked. The only fault was the page: the salutation sits at the foot of page 6 and the quoted sentences are on page 7. Douglass is unshipped, unbanned and at zero for the year, and a letter is not oratory.
